name: Wall Calf Stretch
summary: A static standing stretch performed against a wall to lengthen the gastrocnemius and Achilles tendon complex.

setup: Stand facing a wall approximately arm's length away.
Place both hands flat against the wall around shoulder height.
Step one leg back into a staggered stance, keeping both feet pointed straight ahead.
steps: Keep the rear leg straight and press the back heel firmly flat into the floor.
Bend your front knee and gently shift your weight and hips forward toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the upper calf of the rear leg.
Hold the stretch statically without bouncing.
Step forward to release the tension, then repeat on the opposite leg.
instructions.breathing: Breathe slowly and deeply, allowing the calf muscles to relax further into the stretch with each exhalation.
cues: Drive the back heel into the floor.
Keep the back knee fully straight.

common_faults.fault: Lifting the rear heel off the ground.
common_faults.correction: Shorten your stance so your heel remains firmly anchored to the floor throughout the stretch.
Align the rear foot parallel to the front foot so the calf is stretched evenly.

common_faults.fault: Bouncing or pulsing in and out of the stretch.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a steady, controlled hold to avoid activating the stretch reflex or straining the Achilles tendon.

precautions: Stretch only to the point of mild tension, avoiding sharp pain in the ankle or Achilles tendon.
